final_narrative:
The metabolomics dataset reveals a strong perturbation of **Pyrimidine metabolism** (KEGG map00240), the top-enriched pathway with an extraordinary fold-enrichment and FDR effectively zero. Six of the nine input compounds map to this pathway: deoxyuridine (C00526), CDP (C00112), uridine 5′-monophosphate (C00105), dihydrouracil (C00429), ureidopropionic acid (C02642), and deoxyribose 1-phosphate (C00672).

A driver cluster is centred on the **Pyrimidine catabolism** pathway (Reactome R-HSA-73621), which deoxyuridine, dihydrouracil, and ureidopropionic acid all annotate. KEGG reaction-graph analysis confirms that deoxyuridine (C00526) and dihydrouracil (C00429) are linked bidirectionally via an intermediate (path length 2), indicating deoxyuridine perturbation propagates to its downstream catabolic products. Uridine 5′-monophosphate (C00105) additionally belongs to Reactome's *Metabolism of nucleotides* (R-HSA-15869) and *Pyrimidine salvage* (R-HSA-73614), implicating both anabolic and salvage arms of the network. CDP (C00112) links the network to DNA precursor synthesis via ribonucleotide reduction. Deoxyuridine also maps to three SMPDB disease entries — Beta Ureidopropionase Deficiency (SMP00172), Dihydropyrimidinase Deficiency (SMP00178), and MNGIE (Mitochondrial Neurogastrointestinal Encephalopathy) (SMP00202) — highlighting clinical relevance for nucleotide-catabolism disorders.

**Limitations**: Only six of the nine input metabolites were recovered in the top-enriched pathways. Spironolactone, methionine sulfoxide, and 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid lack annotation in the primary candidate pathways, and their biological role in this dataset remains uncertain without further targeted analysis.
